mainTopic: How the ברייתא, as explained by רבא through כלל ופרט וכלל, reads the פסוק of כפל so that ״גניבה״ makes every stolen item subject to double payment
overview: The ברייתא goes through the פסוק of כפל (שמות 22:3) word by word. Each time, it imagines a shorter פסוק and asks whether the general word ״גניבה״ would then cover only items like the animals listed. That narrow group always turns out to add only something the פסוק already names outright: a sheep, a donkey, or animals through the word ״חיים״. So ״גניבה״ must include every item. The גמרא then challenges the ברייתא's wording 'let it say ox and theft.' Read either way, ox first or theft first, the rules of פרט וכלל and כלל ופרט do not fit what the ברייתא says. רבא explains that the ברייתא counts ״חיים״ as a second general word, which makes the פסוק a כלל ופרט וכלל. When the two general words seem unlike each other, the גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows דבי רבי ישמעאל. רבא then walks through the whole ברייתא again on this reading. It ends by asking why the doubled phrase ״אם המצא תמצא״ is needed, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Since sheep is written, theft must include everything
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the previous round. The limited reading of ״גניבה״ is pushed aside because ״שה״ is written explicitly, so ״גניבה״ must include all items.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says "sheep," a sheep is already stated outright. So what does the word "theft" add? It comes to include every kind of item.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes the earlier question. ״גניבה״ cannot be limited to the narrow group the earlier reading suggested, because that group's only extra member, the sheep, is already written in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא suggested that ״גניבה״ might only add items like the ones listed (things fit for the מזבח), and the only such animal it would add is a sheep. But the פסוק writes ״שה״ outright, so ״גניבה״ would add nothing under that reading. A word in the תורה must teach something, so ״גניבה״ must include every item.

keyTerms.meaning: Sheep (or goat), one of the animals named in the פסוק
It is already stated, meaning the פסוק says it outright
How do I give meaning to this word, or what is it here for?
To include

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern: if the narrow reading of ״גניבה״ would add only something the פסוק already names, the narrow reading falls away and ״גניבה״ includes everything.

phrases.english: When it says "sheep" —
a sheep is already stated,
so what do I do with the word "theft"?
It comes to include every item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the round about ״שה״ that began before this section
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects limiting ״גניבה״ to items like those named, here things fit for the מזבח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The only extra item that reading would add, a sheep, is already written explicitly

steps.title: Why does the verse need to mention donkey?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if ״שור״, ״שה״, and ״גניבה״ were enough to include everything, why write ״חמור״?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say only "ox," "sheep," and "theft," and everything would be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the extra word ״חמור״. If everything is already included, the donkey seems to be wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 just concluded that ״שור״, ״שה״, and ״גניבה״ together cover all items. So the word ״חמור״ looks extra. The ברייתא wants to find what ״חמור״ adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it say, meaning the פסוק could have said just this
Ox
And everything would be included in the general term

phrases.english: Let it say "ox," "sheep," and "theft,"
and everything would be included!
phrases.notes: The question it leaves unspoken: so why write ״חמור״?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 1 to question why ״חמור״ is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״שור״, ״שה״, and ״גניבה״ already include everything, ״חמור״ adds nothing

steps.title: Without donkey, theft would be limited to firstborn-holy animals
steps.stepSummary: The answer: without ״חמור״, we would limit ״גניבה״ to items like ox and sheep, which can have the holiness of a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Had the פסוק been written that way, I would have said: just as the listed items are things that become holy as a firstborn, so too only things that become holy as a firstborn are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that without ״חמור״ we would find a narrower shared feature in ox and sheep. That feature is בכורה holiness, and ״גניבה״ would only reach items that share it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ox and sheep share a trait: a firstborn of either is holy as a בכור. If those were the only examples, ״גניבה״ would be limited to things with that trait. So ״חמור״ is needed to break that narrow reading, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were written this way
I would have said, meaning a mistaken first reading
Just as the detail spelled out has a certain feature, so too only things with that feature are included
Holy with the holiness of a firstborn animal

phrases.english: Had it been so, I would have said:
just as the detail that is spelled out —
is an item that becomes holy as a firstborn,
phrases.notes: "The detail" means the animals listed by name, here ox and sheep.

phrases.english: so too only items that become holy as a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word prevents a mistaken narrow reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״חמור״, ״גניבה״ would cover only items that can have בכורה holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: ״חמור״ is written to push aside that narrow reading

steps.title: Since donkey is written, theft must include everything
steps.stepSummary: The narrow בכורה reading would add only a donkey. But ״חמור״ is written outright, so ״גניבה״ must include every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would that rule add? A donkey. But when the פסוק says "donkey," a donkey is already stated. So what does "theft" add? It comes to include every kind of item.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that once ״חמור״ is written, the בכורה limit is useless. ״גניבה״ therefore includes everything, the same move as in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only other animal with בכורה holiness that the narrow rule would bring in is the donkey. Since the פסוק names the donkey outright, the narrow rule would teach nothing new. So ״גניבה״ must reach all items.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there for you to bring in, meaning what extra item would this rule add?
When it says
So then

phrases.english: What would there be for you to include? A donkey.
phrases.notes: A firstborn donkey also has a holiness, the פטר חמור, so it's the only animal this narrow rule would add.

phrases.english: When it says "donkey" —
a donkey is already stated,
so what do I do with the word "theft"?
It comes to include every item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the round begun in step 2 by knocking out the narrow reading of step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects limiting ״גניבה״ to items with בכורה holiness
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The only extra item that rule would add, a donkey, is already written explicitly

steps.title: Why does the verse need the word alive?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks again: with ״שור״, ״חמור״, ״שה״, and ״גניבה״ everything would be included, so why add more?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say only "ox," "donkey," "sheep," and "theft," and everything would be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a new round. It challenges the next word in the פסוק, ״חיים״, which now looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After step 4, the list plus ״גניבה״ already seems to cover all items. So the last word of the פסוק, ״חיים״, appears to add nothing. The ברייתא now sets out to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkey
Theft, the general word in the פסוק

phrases.english: Let it say "ox," "donkey," "sheep," and "theft" —
and everything would be included!
phrases.notes: The unspoken question this time: so why does the פסוק add the word ״חיים״?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 4 to question the next word, ״חיים״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the three animals plus ״גניבה״ already include everything, ״חיים״ seems extra

steps.title: Without alive, theft would be limited to living creatures
steps.stepSummary: The answer: without ״חיים״, we would limit ״גניבה״ to living creatures, since ox, donkey, and sheep are all animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Had the פסוק been written that way, I would have said: just as the listed items are living creatures, so too only living creatures are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the three named animals share one clear feature: they are alive. So ״גניבה״ would reach only living creatures and not objects. The ברייתא is now setting up how ״חיים״ removes that limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With all three animals listed, the narrow shared feature is now simply being a living creature. That reading would leave out non-living things such as vessels or clothing. The next step shows how ״חיים״ fixes this.

keyTerms.meaning: Living creatures, animals
The detail, meaning the specific items listed by name

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as the final ruling that only animals get כפל. It is the mistaken first reading (״הייתי אומר״) that the ברייתא is about to correct.

phrases.english: Had it been so, I would have said:
just as the detail spelled out is living creatures,
so too only living creatures are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ כָּךְ, הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: מָה הַפְּרָט מְפוֹרָשׁ – בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and sets up the next move about ״חיים״
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word prevents a mistaken narrow reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״חיים״, ״גניבה״ would cover only living creatures
steps.terutzMaskana: ״חיים״ is needed to push aside the limit to living creatures (explained next)

steps.title: The word 'alive' already covers living creatures
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the idea that ״גניבה״ means only living creatures, because the פסוק already says ״חיים״ outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would ״גניבה״ have added? Only other living creatures. But the פסוק already says ״חיים״, so living creatures are stated outright.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the narrow reading from step 6. That reading said ״גניבה״ includes only living creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the narrow reading, ״גניבה״ would only add other animals beyond ox, donkey and sheep. But the פסוק already writes ״חיים״ outright, and that word covers animals, so the narrow reading would teach nothing new. This is the same move the ברייתא made with ״חמור״ in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there for you to include? (what would the extra word add?)
Other living creatures
'Alive', a word in the פסוק of theft
It is already stated

phrases.english: What is there for you to include?
Other living creatures.
When it says "alive,"
phrases.notes: This is the last word of the phrase in שמות 22:3: 'from ox to donkey to sheep, alive.'

phrases.english: living creatures are already stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה יֵשׁ לְךָ לְהָבִיא – שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״חַיִּים״ – הֲרֵי חַיִּים אָמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the narrow 'living creatures only' reading proposed in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that ״גניבה״ is limited to living creatures.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The only extra items that reading would add, other living creatures, are already stated explicitly by the word ״חיים״, so ״גניבה״ would add nothing.

steps.title: The word 'theft' includes every item
steps.stepSummary: Since every narrower reading has been ruled out, ״גניבה״ must include every kind of item in the double payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the word ״גניבה״ for? To include every item.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches its final conclusion. ״גניבה״ teaches that a thief pays double for any item he steals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each narrower meaning of ״גניבה״ was knocked out because the פסוק spells that group out on its own. The first was items that can be holy as a בכור, which is why ״חמור״ is written. The second was living creatures, which is why ״חיים״ is written. The only meaning left is that it covers everything.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I fulfill (give meaning to) this word?
To include
Every item

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's bottom line: ״גניבה״ includes every item. The double payment of a thief applies to any item he steals, not only to animals.

phrases.english: So how do I fulfill "theft"?
To include every item.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״גְּנֵיבָה״? לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion once the last narrow reading has been rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״גניבה״ includes every item in the double payment.

steps.title: The verse puts 'theft' before 'ox'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's line 'let it say ״שור״ and ״גניבה״'. The פסוק actually says ״גניבה״ first and ״שור״ second.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'Let it say ״שור״ and ״גניבה״.' But is ״שור״ and ״גניבה״ written? What is written is ״גניבה״ and then ״שור״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to examine the ברייתא's wording. It points out that the ברייתא listed the words in the wrong order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In learning a כלל and a פרט, the order of the words changes the rule. The ברייתא spoke as if ״שור״ came first, but in the פסוק ״גניבה״ comes first. So the גמרא wants to know what the ברייתא meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it say (only this)
Is it written...? (it is not)
That is written

phrases.english: The Master said:
Let it say "ox" and "theft."
phrases.notes: This quotes an earlier line of the same ברייתא, from before this section.

phrases.english: Is "ox" and "theft" written?
It is "theft" and "ox" that is written!
phrases.notes: The פסוק reads 'הגנבה משור', so 'the theft' comes before 'ox' (שמות 22:3).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי כְּתִיב ״שׁוֹר״ וּ״גְנֵיבָה״? ״גְּנֵיבָה״ וָ״שׁוֹר״ הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line that examines the wording of the ברייתא just completed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The order of the words in the ברייתא does not match the order of the words in the פסוק.

steps.title: Suggestion: the ברייתא means 'if it had said'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא was talking about a made-up case: if the פסוק had said ״שור״ first and then ״גניבה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say the ברייתא means 'if it had said', meaning: if the פסוק had said ״שור״ and then ״גניבה״...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to explain the ברייתא's word order. It is setting up the next move, where this suggestion will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this suggestion, the ברייתא never claimed the פסוק says ״שור״ first. It was only imagining that order. That would remove the problem of the wrong word order.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (a suggestion that is about to be rejected)
If it had been said
He (the ברייתא) is saying

phrases.english: And if you will say it is saying "if it had been said":
if it had said "ox" and "theft";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the word-order challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא as speaking about a made-up case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to claim the פסוק says ״שור״ before ״גניבה״.
steps.terutzMaskana: Possibly the ברייתא only meant 'if the פסוק had said ״שור״ and then ״גניבה״'.

steps.title: Ox first would include everything
steps.stepSummary: If ״שור״ came first, that would be a פרט וכלל, which includes everything. The ברייתא could not then say 'just as the detail is defined'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you then say 'just as the detail is clearly defined'? ״שור״ would be a פרט and ״גניבה״ a כלל. In a פרט וכלל, the כלל adds to the פרט, and everything is included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of step 10. If ״שור״ came first, the ברייתא's next step, limiting things to what is like an ox, would not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for a detail followed by a general term is that the general term widens things to include everything. But the ברייתא went on to say 'just as the detail is defined', which limits things to items like the ox. That limiting step cannot happen in a פרט וכלל, so the suggestion fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say...? (no, you cannot)
Just as the detail is clearly defined (used to limit to similar items)
A detail followed by a general term
The general term adds to the detail (everything is included)

phrases.english: But can you say
"just as the detail is clearly defined"?!
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's earlier step that limited things to items like an ox.

phrases.english: "Ox" is a detail and "theft" is a general term;
a detail and a general term:
the general term becomes an addition to the detail,
and all things are included!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'if it had been said' answer of step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא was talking about a made-up order with ״שור״ first.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A פרט וכלל includes everything, so the ברייתא's limiting step 'מה הפרט מפורש' could not apply.

steps.title: Suggestion: the ברייתא follows the verse's real order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again. Maybe the ברייתא means the words in the order the פסוק really has them: ״גניבה״ and then ״שור״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they mean it as it is written: ״גניבה״ and then ״שור״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to read the ברייתא. This sets up the next step, where this reading will be tested too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since imagining ״שור״ first did not work, the גמרא now reads the ברייתא as following the פסוק's real order. Now the question is whether that order fits the ברייתא's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new suggestion after rejecting the old one)
As it is written
They are saying

phrases.english: Rather, they are saying it as it is written:
"theft" and "ox."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 9 after step 11 rejected the first one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא according to the actual order of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was talking about a made-up order with ״שור״ first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Perhaps the ברייתא means the real order, ״גניבה״ and then ״שור״.

steps.title: Theft first would include only an ox
steps.stepSummary: If ״גניבה״ comes first, that is a כלל ופרט, which includes only what the detail names. That would be only an ox, so the ברייתא's reasoning still does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you then say 'everything is included', or 'just as the detail is clearly defined'? ״גניבה״ is a כלל and ״שור״ is a פרט. In a כלל ופרט, the כלל includes only what is in the פרט. An ox, yes; anything else, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion as well. In the real order, the rule would include only an ox, and that does not match what the ברייתא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general term followed by a detail is limited to exactly what the detail names. It does not include everything, and it does not include items similar to the detail. So neither of the ברייתא's claims works. רבא resolves this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A general term followed by a detail
The general term includes only what is in the detail
Everything is included in the general term
Yes ... no

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two orders. In a פרט וכלל (detail first), everything is included. In a כלל ופרט (general term first), only the exact detail is included. The whole problem in this section comes from which word comes first.

phrases.english: Can you say "everything is included in the general term,"
or "just as the detail is clearly defined"?
"Theft" is a general term and "ox" is a detail;
a general term and a detail:
the general term includes only what is in the detail;
an ox, yes; anything else, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ ״הַכֹּל בַּכְּלָל״, אוֹ ״מָה הַפְּרָט מְפוֹרָשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'as it is written' answer of step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא follows the real order, ״גניבה״ and then ״שור״.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A כלל ופרט limits the rule to an ox alone, which fits neither 'הכל בכלל' nor 'מה הפרט מפורש'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how much the order of the words matters when learning from a כלל and a פרט. It is why רבא, in the next step, has to bring in a third word to explain the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: the word 'alive' makes this a כלל ופרט וכלל
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא counts ״חיים״ as a second כלל, so the פסוק is a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The ברייתא is leaning on the word 'alive'. It is reading the words as a generalization, a detail, and a generalization.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new way to understand the ברייתא, since the earlier attempts did not work. He says the ברייתא counts the word ״חיים״ as another general word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 and 13 failed because two words alone make only a פרט וכלל or a כלל ופרט. רבא adds a third word, ״חיים״, at the end. That gives גניבה (כלל), שור (פרט), חיים (כלל), which is a כלל ופרט וכלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Alive. The word at the end of the פסוק, read here as a second general word.
Relies on, leans on.
A general word, a detail, then another general word. Together they include things similar to the detail.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The tanna is relying on the word 'alive',
and he is calling it a generalization, a detail, and a generalization.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תַּנָּא אַ״חַיִּים״ קָא סָמֵיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a fresh resolution after both earlier answers were rejected in steps 11 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק by adding a third word (״חיים״) to form a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was working with only two words, ״גניבה״ and ״שור״.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא works with three words: גניבה, שור, חיים. That is a כלל ופרט וכלל.

steps.title: The two general words are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״חיים״ is not the same kind of general word as ״גניבה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the last generalization is not like the first generalization!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading. The first general word and the last general word do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״גניבה״ covers anything at all that can be stolen, while ״חיים״ covers only living animals. A כלל ופרט וכלל normally needs two similar general words, so רבא's structure seems not to apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not similar.
The last general word.
The first general word.

phrases.english: But it is not similar:
the last generalization to the first generalization!
phrases.notes: The first one, ״גניבה״, covers everything. The last one, ״חיים״, covers only living things.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא דָּמֵי כְּלָלָא בָּתְרָא לִכְלָלָא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's כלל ופרט וכלל reading from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that ״חיים״ serves as the second כלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כלל ופרט וכלל needs matching כללים, and ״גניבה״ (everything) and ״חיים״ (animals only) do not match.

steps.title: This ברייתא follows the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא comes from דבי רבי ישמעאל, who learns a כלל ופרט וכלל even when the two כללים differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא is from the school of רבי ישמעאל, who learns generalizations and details even in a case like this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the author of this ברייתא holds that the two general words do not have to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed a rule that both כללים must be alike. דבי רבי ישמעאל does not require that, so for this ברייתא רבא's כלל ופרט וכלל still works.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (students) of רבי ישמעאל.
In a case like this.
Expounds, learns out from the פסוק.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules of כלל ופרט are not applied the same way by everyone. Who wrote a ברייתא can decide whether a structure applies.

phrases.aramaic: הָא תַּנָּא – דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא,
phrases.english: This tanna is from the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
who expounds generalizations and details in a case like this.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific school with its own approach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כלל ופרט וכלל requires two matching כללים.
steps.terutzMaskana: דבי רבי ישמעאל learns a כלל ופרט וכלל even when the כללים differ.

steps.title: רבא explains what the ברייתא found difficult
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא's real difficulty is the doubled phrase ״אם המצא תמצא״. To reach it, he goes back over the ברייתא from the start, beginning with the question of why the פסוק lists more than ״שור״, ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what bothered the תנא: Why do I need 'if it shall surely be found'? Let the פסוק say 'ox', 'theft' and 'alive', and everything would be included!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא first names the question the ברייתא ends with: why ״אם המצא תמצא״ is needed. He then walks through the ברייתא from the beginning using his new reading. Its first question is why the פסוק needs more than ״שור״, ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On רבא's reading, ״גניבה״ (כלל), ״שור״ (פרט) and ״חיים״ (כלל) would already form a כלל ופרט וכלל, so the other animals in the list look extra. The ברייתא explains each extra animal in turn. Only at the very end (step 25) does it come back to the question of ״אם המצא תמצא״.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for him.
'If it shall surely be found.' The doubled verb at the start of the פסוק.
Why do I need it?
Everything is included in the general word.

phrases.english: And this is what is difficult for him:
Why do I need 'If it shall surely be found'?
Let it say 'ox' and 'theft' and 'alive',
and everything would be included!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the כלל ופרט וכלל reading stands, רבא uses it to explain the ברייתא's question from the start.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explaining the ברייתא's question to fit the new reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's line 'let it say ox and theft' could not be explained (steps 9 to 13).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is asking why extra words are needed beyond a three-word כלל ופרט וכלל that would already include everything.

steps.title: Without the extra words, only altar animals would be included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that with only the three words, we would include just things offered on the מזבח. Since ״שה״ is written separately, ״גניבה״ must come to include every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, I would have said: just as the detail (ox) is something offered on the altar, so too only things offered on the altar are included. But what would that add? A sheep. Yet the פסוק already says 'sheep'. So how do I fulfill 'theft'? It comes to include every kind of item.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the ברייתא's answer to the question from the last step. It shows why the פסוק is written the way it is, and concludes that every item is included in כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A three-word כלל ופרט וכלל would include only things like an ox, meaning things offered on the מזבח. The only extra thing that would add is a sheep, and the פסוק already names ״שה״ on its own. So ״גניבה״ must teach something more: every kind of item.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were so.
Something offered on the altar.
Sheep (or goat).
How do I give meaning to (a word)?
To include every item.

steps.whatToRemember: Through רבא's reading of the ברייתא as a כלל ופרט וכלל, the extra words in the פסוק teach that the double payment of a thief applies to every kind of stolen item, not only to animals fit for the מזבח.

phrases.english: If so, I would have said:
Just as the detail is clearly defined
as an item offered on the altar,
so too anything offered on the altar.
What is there to include? 'Sheep'.
When it says 'sheep', sheep is already stated,
so how do I fulfill 'theft'?
To include every item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק needs more than ״שור״, ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Those three words alone would include only animals offered on the מזבח. Since ״שה״ is stated separately, ״גניבה״ must include every item.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כפל applies to all stolen items.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need to say donkey?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: why not write only ״גניבה״, ״שור״, ״שה״ and ״חיים״? Then everything would be included without ״חמור״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say just 'theft', 'ox', 'sheep' and 'alive', and everything would be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks why the word ״חמור״ (donkey) is needed. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18 the ברייתא explained why ״שה״ is needed. Now it moves to the next word, ״חמור״. The claim is that the shorter list would still make a כלל ופרט וכלל that includes everything, so ״חמור״ looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it say: the פסוק could have been written like this
And everything would be included
Donkey

phrases.english: Let it say "theft" and "ox"
and "sheep" and "alive", and everything would be included!
phrases.notes: Notice the list skips ״חמור״. That missing word is what the ברייתא is asking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'why is this word needed' pattern to the next word, ״חמור״.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word ״חמור״ add to the פסוק?

steps.title: Without donkey we would limit it to firstborn-type animals
steps.stepSummary: Without ״חמור״, the details ״שור״ and ״שה״ would teach us to include only things that can have the holiness of a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were written that way, I would say: just as the details are things that become holy as a firstborn, so too only things that become holy as a firstborn are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by showing what we would wrongly think without the word ״חמור״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a כלל ופרט וכלל, we include only items that are like the details. ״שור״ and ״שה״ both share the holiness of a בכור, so the group would be just things with בכורה holiness. That limit would leave most stolen items out of כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as the detail is clearly defined: the start of the comparison to the details
The holiness of a firstborn animal
Had it been so

phrases.english: Had it been so, I would have said:
Just as the detail is clearly defined
as something that becomes holy as a firstborn,
phrases.notes: The details here are ox and sheep, and both have the holiness of a firstborn.

phrases.english: so too only things that become holy as a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by showing the wrong limit we would have made.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without ״חמור״, the law would be limited to things with בכורה holiness.

steps.title: Donkey is written, so theft includes everything
steps.stepSummary: The only extra item that group would add is a donkey. The donkey is already written out, so ״גניבה״ must come to include every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would that add? A donkey. But since the פסוק says 'donkey', a donkey is already stated. So what do I learn from 'theft'? It includes every item.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes this round. Since ״חמור״ is written out on its own, the narrow group is pointless, so ״גניבה״ must include everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'firstborn' group would only add one thing beyond ox and sheep: a donkey. The פסוק already names the donkey, so the details cannot be there just to teach that group. So the כלל ״גניבה״ must be read as broadly as possible: every item.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there for you to include?
It is already stated
How do I give meaning to this word?
To include every kind of item

phrases.english: What is there for you to include? A donkey.
phrases.notes: A firstborn donkey also has a kind of firstborn holiness, so it is the one extra item that group would add.

phrases.english: When it says "donkey,"
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets aren't in every version; they're added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: a donkey is already stated.
So how do I give meaning to "theft"?
To include every item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the narrow group from Step 20 adds nothing, so ״גניבה״ must be read broadly.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because ״חמור״ is written out, ״גניבה״ includes every item for כפל.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק need extra words beyond the list with donkey?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks again: write ״גניבה״, ״שור״, ״שה״, ״חמור״, ״חיים״, and everything would be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say just 'theft', 'ox', 'sheep', 'donkey' and 'alive', and everything would be included!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks the same kind of question again, now with ״חמור״ in the list. This sets up the next answer about what ״חיים״ adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that ״חמור״ is explained, the ברייתא checks whether this fuller list would be enough. If it would, the remaining words of the פסוק would look extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Theft: the first כלל in the פסוק

phrases.english: Let it say "theft," and "ox," and "sheep,"
and "donkey," and "alive", and everything would be included!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the pattern one level up, now with ״חמור״ in the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What would this fuller list teach, and is anything still missing?

steps.title: With that list we would include only animals
steps.stepSummary: Ox, sheep and donkey are all living animals, so we would include all animals but not objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were written that way, I would say: just as the details are animals, so too all animals are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows the new wrong conclusion we would reach: only animals get כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ״חמור״ is added, the details no longer share firstborn holiness. They do share being living creatures. So the group would widen to all animals, but objects like clothing or money would still be left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Living creatures, animals

phrases.english: Had it been so, I would have said:
Just as the detail is clearly defined as animals,
so too all animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילּוּ כֵּן, הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר: מָה הַפְּרָט מְפוֹרָשׁ – בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22 with a new, wider but still limited group.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The list would include all animals but not objects.

steps.title: Animals are already written, so theft includes everything
steps.stepSummary: That group would only add other animals. ״חיים״ already covers animals, so ״גניבה״ must include every item.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would that add? Other animals. But since the פסוק says 'alive', animals are already stated. So what do I learn from 'theft'? It includes every item.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes this round the same way as before. Animals are already covered by ״חיים״, so ״גניבה״ must reach all items, even objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'animals' group would only add other animals, and the word ״חיים״ already covers them. A פרט that teaches nothing new cannot be what limits the law. So the כלל ״גניבה״ includes even objects.

keyTerms.meaning: Other animals, beyond the ones listed
'Alive': the second כלל in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern each time: without the extra word, the details would make a narrow group. That group is already written out, so ״גניבה״ includes everything.

phrases.aramaic: מָה יֵשׁ לְךָ לְהָבִיא – שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים;
phrases.english: What is there for you to include? Other animals.
When it says "alive," living things are already stated.
So how do I give meaning to "theft"?
To include every item.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה יֵשׁ לְךָ לְהָבִיא – שְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the animal group from Step 23 adds nothing, so ״גניבה״ includes everything.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ״גניבה״ includes every item, even objects, for כפל.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say "if it shall surely be found"?
steps.stepSummary: If ״גניבה״ already includes everything, the doubled phrase ״אם המצא תמצא״ seems to have no job.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'if it shall surely be found'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks what the doubled words ״אם המצא תמצא״ are for. This question sets up the next part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything has already been included through ״גניבה״. So the doubled wording ״המצא תמצא״ looks extra, and it must have its own job to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it shall surely be found': the doubled phrase in the פסוק of כפל
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: Why do I need "if it shall surely be found"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since ״גניבה״ now includes everything, the remaining extra phrase needs a reason. This is the question רבא said in step 17 was bothering the תנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״גניבה״ already covers every item, the doubled phrase seems to teach nothing.
